I was browsing fph all the way back during the reddit days and enjoyed every moment I was making fun of fatties. I did it as a slim guy who was repulsed at fat people eating so much. I usually had a BMI around 19, and simply could not understand how fat people ate so much. Then about 5 months ago, I started going to the gym and cataloged my eating habits briefly. I realized I hated eating a lot to gain muscle and that fat people just eat until they feel sick all the time, or at least did at some point in their life and got used to it.

Here I am now 5'3.5" and weighing 135 with a body fat percentage of about 12%, to where all my friends have seen my transformation and I get comments akin to "looking pretty buff", "man, you're hitting the gym pretty hard", etc. Part of why I did this was to get healthy. The other part was I was fucking sick of (fat) people seeing me eat during my binge days, and complaining about how thin people with fast metabolisms can eat as much as they want and not gain weight. I had to prove to myself and everyone that it was not true, and if you eat, you gain weight. In my case, I lifted weights as well so that I gained muscle mass.

Now here's the kicker, I rent an apartment and have an overweight roommate. I also have another roommate who just moved in who is literally a body builder with ~9% body fat. Guy is shredded, and often walks around without a shirt on. My fat roommate comes out one day and says (I shit you not), "fuck man, can't you put a shirt on? Seeing you makes me realize what a fat fuck I am." and then proceeds to literally beg the bodybuilding roommate to train him. Best part is he refused, and instead went to the gym with me to help me test my 1RM for my squat (I squatted 185 fine, but failed at 200).

Another example is I have an office mate (overweight, and gross) who saw me drinking my fruit+nuts smoothie. I finished it, then said I was leaving to the gym, and she said "oh I hadn't even noticed you work out! healthy life style" in a flirtatious tone. Yuck. I just keep talking about how it's a choice to be fit and fat shame.

How would I quantify how my hatred of fatties evolved? First it was repulsion from lack of understanding. Then it was repulsion by understanding, and my hatred magnified. Now it's evolving into passive fat shaming, by sheer fact that I exist. Remember, the fitter you are, the more easily you fat shame people. And I will continue to get even fitter, not to shame them, but to feel good. And the auto-shaming is a great bonus.

My favorite part of gaining weight out of spite is I have two friends who are identical heights to me. One is higher body fat than the other, but both are overweight. And I repeatedly rubbed it in their faces every milestone of my way. "How much do you weigh? .... oh 130? That's my target weight now." Then surpass them "I weigh more than you now, how does that make you feel?" It's going to be hard to catch up to my friend who is 5'3" and 150 lbs, but god dammit I'm going to try. If I can make it I'll shame the ever living shit out of him over it.

Sitting here with a BMI of 23-24 and eating 2500 calories a day trying to gain more weight. One of my favorite parts of this is how this is my new lifestyle, and all my friends (some overweight) saw me transform, and I can shame them by asking them to go to the gym with me and they can't say shit about it, since they see the results I have and they know it works.

Sorry for the disjointed post, I just wanted to say a lot haha.
